- One seed has a distinct **purple/violet stain** on it

**Analysis:**

The test image shows an opened soybean pod with 3 seeds, one of which has a prominent **purple/violet stain**. There is also some white material and pod interior discoloration.

Comparison against references:
- **Purple_Seed_Stain**: Bottom-right panel shows an opened pod held by hand with a seed displaying the same purple stain — near-perfect match
- **Cercospora**: Leaf symptoms only (purple spots on leaves) — no seed involvement
- **White_Mold**: Fluffy white mycelium on stems/pods — doesn't match
- **Diaporthe/Phomopsis**: Pod/stem lesions, no purple stain
- **Anthracnose**: Dark acervuli on pods, circular lesions — doesn't match

The distinguishing feature — purple/violet seed discoloration inside an opened pod — is the hallmark of Purple Seed Stain (caused by *Cercospora kikuchii*).
